one_line: A local construction schedule editor that an agent can read and modify.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central because structured access to local dependency state and recalculation is materially safer and more precise than screen automation, especially under privacy constraints.
leverage_evidence: Packet states schedules stay in browser IndexedDB and CPM recalculates locally.
Frame sheets show registered tools, local-data claims, Gantt/network views, and an agent panel.
execution_rationale: The frame sheets show a coherent scheduling product and an evolving agent-assisted workflow, though the exact edit-to-ripple result is not crisply demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Frames show schedule activities, dependency connectors, timeline bars, and agent/tool panels.
Frame sheet includes claims of seven tools and zero schedule data sent externally.
impact_rationale: Construction teams have a real need to understand schedule float and dependency impacts while protecting sensitive project data.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies delivery dates, subcontractors, and cost structure as sensitive schedule information.
Product targets critical-path scheduling and activity movement.
creativity_rationale: The combination of browser-local critical-path scheduling, privacy preservation, and an agent that operates a graph rather than a list is a notably original interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Concept explicitly treats construction schedules as dependency graphs and agents as schedule operators.
Privacy constraint is integrated into the product rationale.
usability_note: The schedule editor and visual dependency model appear usable; agent workflow details are somewhat small in the frames.
red_flags: Contact sheets repeat static explanatory screens and small UI text is difficult to verify.
advance_reason: One of the clearest cases where structured in-page tools materially change a sensitive, stateful workflow.

one_line: A revision-aware agent witness system for validating identity mapping rules before save.
what_it_does: Stages rules, finds minimal synthetic witness users, explains violations, invalidates stale evidence after edits, and prepares a fresh review packet while humans control confirmation and apply.
leverage_rationale: The structured tool surface is indispensable to safely reason over draft state, revisions, rule semantics, minimal witnesses, and stale evidence; DOM-driving cannot replicate this reliably.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes five strict WebMCP tools: read, stage, find, preview, prepare.
Revision-bound evidence turns stale after edits, and applying remains a page control outside the tool list.
execution_rationale: Transcript and frames together show a complete, intentional workflow from staging through witness discovery, edit invalidation, rechecking, and green review packet.
execution_evidence: Transcript walks through three rules, witness users, receipts, revision 19, stale evidence, refinements, and green lights.
Video frame sheets show the product workflow and review states.
impact_rationale: Identity administrators have a serious need to prevent silent account/group mapping errors before production changes, and the product directly addresses that risk.
impact_evidence: Transcript gives concrete contractor, manager-null, and HR precedence failures.
Human approval and no-save-tool boundary preserve control over identity changes.
creativity_rationale: Minimal witness-set discovery plus revision-bound proof and stale-evidence invalidation is a genuinely novel interaction model pursued deeply.
creativity_evidence: Smallest synthetic set that trips every rule is computed and shown.
Freshness of every proof is treated as a first-class state.
usability_note: The staged cards, receipts, revision badge, and green/red evidence states make a complex safety workflow legible.
red_flags: Claims are based on a narrated demo rather than independently observed live use.
standouts: Clear evidence of actual agent invocation and result handling.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage, complete demonstrated workflow, and unusually original evidence semantics.
